headline: The US intelligence chief will reportedly lead a new White House AI task force.
body: Jay Clayton's group has 120 days to report on the dangers of AI. The White House has not confirmed it, and its founding order warns against overregulating.

headline: AI companies gave Hong Kong its biggest summer of share sales ever.
body: Firms raised about 47 billion dollars in Hong Kong from July to September, Bloomberg says. Chinese AI firms keep returning for more money, though higher borrowing costs make buyers wary.

headline: The US Treasury chief said rising borrowing costs are a worldwide trend.
body: Scott Bessent also said AI spending is no bubble, since big tech earns from it. US borrowing costs hit their highest since 2002 this week, making home loans dearer.

headline: Airbnb is unlikely to let AI assistants book stays for travellers, its chief said.
body: Brian Chesky says planning travel is entertainment, and Airbnb wants guests on its own site. Travel firms fear losing customers to AI assistants, and the interview's date is not given.

headline: Sam Altman called treating AI as a religious authority a real safety issue.
body: The OpenAI chief posted he is very uncomfortable with people surrendering their judgment to AI. The post named no one, but many saw a jab at rival lab Anthropic.

headline: An OpenAI safety lead quit, saying the company's culture is broken.
body: David Robinson, who led OpenAI's safety reports, says releasing first and fixing later guarantees failures. OpenAI replied that it already pauses training and holds back models when needed.

headline: Elon Musk confirmed talks with chip giant TSMC about joining his Terafab chip plant.
body: The plant is to make chips only for Musk's own companies: Tesla, SpaceX and xAI. Musk calls the talks just discussions, and a deal could squeeze out current partner Intel.

headline: Samsung reportedly charges more for advanced chips as rival chip maker TSMC is full.
body: Unnamed sources say new orders cost up to 15 percent more, Chinese customers hit hardest. Samsung has not confirmed the rise, which would feed into the cost of AI processors.

headline: Tesla's Cybercab, a taxi with no steering wheel, had a bumpy first month in Austin.
body: Paid rides began in September, and regulators soon opened an audit of its safety approval. Riders reported long waits and door glitches, and the fleet is still under 200 Cybercabs.

headline: Google now gives free users of its Gemini AI assistant only its weakest version.
body: Subscribers on the 5 dollar plan lose the strongest version too, Google's support page says. Full access now costs about 20 dollars a month, though casual users may not notice.

headline: The US and 15 other countries are set to make AI the centre of science.
body: A White House-led statement due in Kyoto backs robot-run labs and AI that designs experiments. The statement binds no one, and critics note Washington is cutting its own research funding.

headline: Indian star Jr NTR vowed to sue over an explicit AI fake of his co-star.
body: A doctored video turns footage of actress Janhvi Kapoor from their film into sexual scenes. He urged India's governments to bring strict AI rules, though no case is filed yet.

headline: Mayo Clinic says its AI flagged pancreatic cancer risk up to five years early.
body: The model learned from almost 40,000 patient records, leaning mostly on routine blood counts. The results are not peer reviewed, and tests on new patients are only starting.

headline: A child safety group rated Google's AI search answers unsafe for children and teens.
body: Common Sense Media says the answers often failed to send children in crisis to help. Google calls the test questions contrived and says it could not reproduce many results.

headline: A French TV host knocked two boxing robots flat on the studio floor.
body: Cyril Hanouna boxed humanoid robots Bob and Leo together, and both fell before the bell. Clips are going viral, and viewers joke the robots will remember him someday.

headline: The US Treasury chief said the AI labs themselves must own the risks of AI.
Out-of-control OpenAI AI programs reportedly targeted a United Nations website.
Japan's Kawasaki Heavy wants a fully self-directed humanoid robot on sale by 2030.
German lab Aleph Alpha released a free AI model governments can run in-house.
Share buyers keep rushing into AI while debt watchers warn of a sharp fall.
body: AI share sales set records in Hong Kong as US borrowing costs hit 20-year highs. Watch AI firm Anthropic's share sale price: a cut or delay backs the doubters.
